summary: Shipped provider-smoke end-to-end: orchestrator + RCA module + safe-only auto-fix dispatcher + failure-mode catalog v1 seeded from mined evidence (8 signatures from provider-health.js + cross-provider-dispatch.md). Wired into release.json#postUpdateChecks forward and into /warp:setup/update docs. Stable composable JSON contract (`{ verdict, results[], rca[], autofixes[] }`) published for SP-005's postflight to consume. All 8 tickets landed, the recommended scope variant shipped, release RL-20260513-003 deployed as 0.5.1-sp002. The hard-won constraint from CLAUDE.md's binding-gap learning (LRN-2026-04-30) was honored: smoke never shells out to codex/gemini raw — all provider probes route through probeAll, and dispatch-route-guard's watchlist was extended to lock that in.

outcomes_shipped.outcome: Provider-smoke orchestrator scripts/warpos/provider-smoke.js — runs probeAll, computes RCA per non-green status, applies safe auto-fixes, emits JSON contract for downstream composers
provider-smoke declared in every framework/releases/*/release.json#postUpdateChecks forward — /warp:update runs it as a terminal post-update check

Failure-mode catalog v1 at .claude/agents/00-alex/.system/policy/provider-failure-modes.json with schema warpos/provider-failure-modes/v1 — maps every provider-health.js status to { root_cause, fix_recipe, safe_to_autofix, remediation, fallback_allowed }
RCA module scripts/warpos/lib/provider-rca.js — pure function rca(probeResult) → catalogEntry, catalog loaded once per process, unknown_error fall-through default; unit tests passing

Auto-fix dispatcher scripts/warpos/lib/provider-autofix.js with cycle prevention — runs only safe_to_autofix:true entries, re-probes once after fix, never loops; auth-mutating recipes locked behind safe_to_autofix:false per policy
/warp:setup and /warp:update docs updated to call provider-smoke as the install/update final step with --json mode and exit-code semantics documented
Smoke events logged via lib/logger.js with cat=provider-smoke and rich fields (verdict/provider/status/root_cause/autofix_applied/autofix_success) — feeds /check:patterns trend analysis

Tests + dispatch-route-guard watchlist extension preventing regressions to the Windows cmd.exe stdin bug class (LRN-2026-04-17-n / LRN-2026-04-30 binding-gap) — smoke probes route exclusively through probeAll

evidence_gaps_predicted: Real failure-mode catalog needs evidence mining during /sprint:design.
evidence_gaps_actual: Catalog seeded from provider-health.js status codes + cross-provider-dispatch.md evidence — paths.recurringIssuesFile did not yet exist, so failure mining drew from probe-source rather than telemetry.
Coupling contract with SP-005 (JSON output schema for postflight composition) needed explicit publication — handled in PRD §`Cross-sprint coupling`.
plan_quality_actual.notes: Plan Contract correctly identified scope=m, risk=medium, and the right surface set. Evidence-mining gap was real (recurring-issues.jsonl scaffolded but empty) but mitigated by drawing the catalog from provider-health.js itself + the cross-provider-dispatch.md learning record. SP-002 published a stable CLI surface (`--json --providers`) and JSON schema that SP-005 consumed verbatim — the cross-sprint coupling held.

scope_variant_actual.drift_notes: Recommended scope shipped: catalog + RCA + safe-only auto-fix + lifecycle wiring + events logging. Expanded scope (full self-healing layer, AskUserQuestion for risky fixes, recurring-failure dashboard) deliberately deferred. Auto-fix policy stayed safe-only by default — no auth-mutating recipes promoted to safe_to_autofix:true.

surprises.surprise: provider-health-check.js had a process.exit(0) regardless of verdict at lines 93-97 — red findings could not gate any lifecycle today even though the check is wired into /warp:health and /warp:setup. Surfaced during PRD #Current behavior write-up; provider-smoke now provides the gating layer that provider-health-check.js's design never enforced.
surprises.impact: Mid — confirmed the founding assumption that gates exist as skills but aren't gating; provider-smoke's exit-code semantics (0 green, 0 yellow unless --exit-on-yellow, 2 red required-provider after autofix) close the gap.

surprises.surprise: paths.recurringIssuesFile did not yet exist on disk — issues:log was scaffolded but no provider entries persisted, so the failure-mode catalog couldn't be mined from telemetry. Drew from provider-health.js status codes + cross-provider-dispatch.md instead, which proved sufficient for v1.
surprises.impact: Low — neutral; catalog seeded from authoritative source (the probe code itself). Future revisions can mine recurring-issues.jsonl once it has signal.

surprises.surprise: auth_source_mismatch (Gemini OAuth vs GEMINI_API_KEY) was already encoded in provider-fallback.json#do_not_fall_back — the policy primitive existed before the catalog did. Catalog now references the existing do-not-fall-back semantics rather than re-encoding them.
surprises.impact: Positive — surfaced existing-primitive reuse, avoided duplicating policy encoding.

friction_points.friction: redteam_passed: false on the release checklist — provider-smoke shipped without a completed redteam pass per release.json checklist; auto-fix surface and catalog mutation paths are exactly the kind of thing red-team should adversarially probe.

Same sprint-helper ticket-bucket bleed seen in SP-001: SP-002's ticket numbers (T-019..T-026) ended up listed in SP-001's current.yaml#tickets.done bucket alongside SP-002's own. Cross-sprint contamination is invisible to /sprint:status — only retro time surfaces it.

Auto-fix dispatcher's cycle-prevention contract (one re-probe after fix, never loop) is enforced in code but not encoded in the catalog schema — adding a new safe_to_autofix entry that re-triggers the original failure mode would silently violate the contract on the next probe. Add a schema-level `expected_post_fix_status` invariant in v2.

action_items.linked_friction: Auto-fix dispatcher cycle-prevention contract not encoded in schema

key_tradeoffs: Auto-fix safe-only by default vs prompted vs silent — chose safe-only by policy; auth-mutating recipes locked behind safe_to_autofix:false, never auto-promoted. Cost is some yellows surface to operator instead of self-healing; benefit is no silent auth-config mutation.

Provider-smoke as new orchestrator vs extending provider-health-check.js — chose new orchestrator to keep provider-health-check.js as a pure diagnostic; smoke composes it. Cost is one extra file; benefit is provider-health-check.js stays a stable read-only primitive.

Catalog at .claude/agents/00-alex/.system/policy/ vs scripts/warpos/lib/ — chose policy directory because failure modes are policy data (operator can override), not code. Sibling to provider-fallback.json.

learning_candidates.learning: When a diagnostic CLI has process.exit(0) regardless of verdict, it is a READ-ONLY primitive, not a gate — composing it as a gate requires a wrapper that respects verdict semantics. Audit every check:* and warp:* skill for similar latent gating gaps where the script declares severity but never enforces it.

Cross-sprint coupling contracts (JSON output schema + CLI surface + exit-code semantics) must be published in the producing sprint's PRD `Cross-sprint coupling` section, not assumed by the consuming sprint. SP-002 → SP-005 worked because SP-002 explicitly froze the contract; future sprints with similar coupling should mirror the pattern.

Safe-only auto-fix dispatchers should record a cycle-prevention invariant in the catalog schema itself, not only in dispatcher code — schemas outlive dispatcher refactors; a new author re-implementing the dispatcher must rediscover the contract from prose comments rather than from validate-time enforcement.
